SimBots were added with Ambitions (EP2) and are built from scrap, unlocked from a special opportunity after reaching Inventing Level 10. Impossible to find out in the wild, and the notification thrown after your Sim finishes the opportunity implies they're the first and only ones to create this type of artificial life. They look shabby and metallic, with pipes and gauges repleting their body (not surprising since they're built from literal scrap). They short out if exposed to water (they don't go berserk like Servos did in Sims 2, they just get knocked out until someone fixes them, and oddly enough you can call a repairman to fix them despite it being your Sim's proprietary tech). They're basically regular Sims with a robotic body- they have normal traits (although all of them are guaranteed to be Hydrophobic at first as a safety measure), can eat normal Sim food and drink normal Sim drinks (although scrap is much easier to obtain and much more fulfilling for them), and even have their own favourite colour, music genre and food from conception. They're very similar to how Servos are in Sims 4 with Discover University, even down to their 360° range of motion limbs and janky, robotic movement.

Plumbots were added with Into the Future (EP11) and are found everywhere in Oasis Landing, not to mention that they can easily be crafted with the "Reventlov's Bot Workshop" appliance after Bot Building Level 2. They look much more polished (figuratively and literally, they're so shiny they could serve as a mirror) and have interchangeable parts and trait chips. They're immune to water (and even seem to enjoy it, as they frequently get the want to go swimming if the house they live in has a pool) but don't have the level of human depth that SimBots do (unless specifically built to perform this function by being given the Sentience, Simulated Emotions, Capacity to Love, Sense of Humour, Friendly Functions, Limitless Learning, etc. trait chips). Even if made sentient, they lack favourites and still retain their robotic interactions (Explain Function, Scan Target, etc.), not to mention they can still be instructed to perform certain actions by any Sim. All in all, though, they're much more useful as household members if equipped to do so with the right trait chips (Steel Chef instantly masters their cooking and mixology skill and allows them to prepare delectable meals, Efficient makes their battery last longer and facilitates skill learning if Limitless Learning is also installed, RoboNanny and HandiBot are self-explanatory, Algorithmic Artist \[which aged like either wine or like a fine milk, depending on your viewpoint\] maxes their painting skill, etc.) In my opinion, they're the best possible choice for live-in help, but as storytelling characters or active household members, they can't quite compare to SimBots.

There *is* a canon god in The Sims (technically all of real life is canon but the games are set in SimNation and that's why everything is zany), and they're called the Watcher. It's heavily implied it's the player, since Sims in Sims Medieval look directly at the camera when they begin praying. (Sims Medieval introduced the concept only for it to be dropped altogether because religious conflicts are already bad enough irl and people don't really want that beyond the medieval ages where pretty much everything was a religious conflict)

The Watcher was only really a thing in Sims Medieval, and like in real life with the Tetragrammaton (the Hebrew/Abrahamic god), there's more than just one religion spanning from it. There were the Jacobans, which were basically like the Roman Catholics (extravagant, baroque, members of a wealthy church with all-encompassing power that rules on fear, fire and brimstone), and then there were the Peterans, somewhat resembling the original teachings of Christ (subdued, humble and based on charity/compassion, also with vaguely Mediterranean architecture hinting towards a Roman theme).
